introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2, subject code 0575. Time allowed: two and a half hours.

Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three.

Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory to all candidates, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions; if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions).

All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Tambe has only 12,000 FCFA to organise a birthday party for the son. He invites $x$ adults and $y$ children. Given that:

He uses 1000 FCFA to entertain an adult and 500 FCFA for a child.
incertitudes: Q5 : echelle imprimee « 1 cm pour 1 unite sur l'axe des x et 1 cm pour 4 unites sur l'axe des y » ; lue telle quelle (le « 4 » est net sur le scan). Points imprimes 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 = 8, conformes. Le numero « 5 » de la question est coupe sur le bord gauche du scan ; numero deduit de la suite 4, 6.
Q5(b) : « must not » est imprime « most not » (faute d'impression), recopie « must not ». Le trace est a faire par le candidat : decrit dans le corrige (droites, sommets, region).

questions.corrige_markdown:
Cost of entertaining $x$ adults: $1000x$ FCFA. Cost for $y$ children: $500y$ FCFA.

Tambe has only $12\,000$ FCFA, so the total cost cannot exceed this amount:

$$
1000x+500y\le 12\,000
$$

Divide every term by $500$:

$$
2x+y\le 24
$$

which is the required inequality. $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) The number of children must not be more than the number of adults.

(ii) Write down an inequality in terms of $x$ and $y$ that satisfies this condition. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The number of children $y$ is at most the number of adults $x$:

**$y\le x$.**

(Also $x\ge 0$ and $y\ge 0$, since numbers of people cannot be negative.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
On a graph paper, taking $1$ cm to represent $1$ unit on the $x$-axis and $1$ cm to represent $4$ units on the $y$-axis,

(iii) shade so as to leave unshaded the region represented by these inequalities. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Boundary lines**

- $2x+y=24$, i.e. $y=24-2x$: it passes through $(0,24)$ and $(12,0)$ (also $(8,8)$). Draw a solid line, since the inequality is $\le$.
- $y=x$: it passes through $(0,0)$, $(8,8)$ and $(12,12)$. Draw a solid line.

**Which side to leave unshaded**

- $2x+y\le24$: test the origin, $0\le24$ is true, so the wanted side is the side containing the origin. Shade the side above and to the right of the line $2x+y=24$.
- $y\le x$: test $(4,1)$, $1\le4$ is true, so the wanted side is below the line $y=x$ (towards the $x$-axis). Shade the side above the line $y=x$.
- $x\ge0$ and $y\ge0$: the axes bound the region, so shade the region left of the $y$-axis and below the $x$-axis too.

**Scale:** $x$-axis: $1$ cm for $1$ unit (from $0$ to $12$, so $12$ cm). $y$-axis: $1$ cm for $4$ units (from $0$ to $24$, so $6$ cm).

**Result:** shade everything outside the triangle with vertices $O(0,0)$, $(12,0)$ and $(8,8)$. The unshaded region is this triangle (the vertex $(8,8)$ is the intersection of $y=x$ and $2x+y=24$, since $3x=24$ gives $x=8$).

questions.enonce_markdown: (iv) Hence, find the greatest number of persons to be invited for the party. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The number of persons invited is $x+y$ with $x,\,y$ whole numbers in the unshaded triangle $O(0,0)$, $(12,0)$, $(8,8)$.

Check the vertices:

| Vertex | $x+y$ |
|---|---|
| $(0,0)$ | $0$ |
| $(12,0)$ | $12$ |
| $(8,8)$ | $16$ |

The largest value is at $(8,8)$. Other whole-number points such as $(9,6)$ give only $15$ and $(10,4)$ gives $14$.

Cost check: $1000(8)+500(8)=12\,000$ FCFA, exactly the money available.

**The greatest number of persons is $16$ ($8$ adults and $8$ children).**
